subject: DPA: hybrid geofence + snapshot erasure safeguards — redline Q&A
messages:
From: Svenja Müller <svenja.mueller@acme-payments.de>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: privacy@acme-payments.de
Date: 2028-08-21T09:12:00Z
Subject: Questions on geofence+snapshot clauses in DPA v3

Hi Olga,

Thanks for sending over DPA v3. Our legal team is reviewing the retention and deletion language and had a couple of follow-ups specifically around how Redwood handles snapshots and hybrid residency (we run a private VPC + optional hosted fallback). The two items we need clarified for our counsel: 

1) Snapshots/replicas: the draft says "customer data may be replicated for backup and disaster recovery." We need explicit timing for scheduled snapshots, the region(s) those backups are stored in, and a maximum time-to-erasure for snapshot remnants after a customer-triggered delete or an on-demand erasure request (including backups/restores).

2) Hybrid/residency fallback: our architecture relies on a private deployment in our Frankfurt region but allows automatic fallback to Redwood-hosted capacity in the same EU geofence only. We need contractual guarantees that fallback instances will not store replicas outside the EU and that ephemeral KV caches are treated as transient and not subject to longer retention.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept: (a) a 30-day maximum for snapshot remnants in backups (unless lawfully required to retain), (b) a contract clause requiring all backups and snapshots to remain within the EU geofence, and (c) a definition of which runtime caches are "ephemeral" vs "persistent"?

I've attached our redlines to v3 and a short summary from legal. Happy to hop on a quick call if that's easier.

Regards,
Svenja Müller
Head of Data Privacy — Acme Payments GmbH
[Attachment: ACME_DPA_v3_redline.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: Svenja Müller <svenja.mueller@acme-payments.de>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-21T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on geofence+snapshot clauses in DPA v3

Hi Svenja — thanks, and appreciate the clear redlines. Looping in Laura (legal) and Markus (runtime infra) to confirm technical and contractual details. High-level answers below; Laura/Markus: please confirm or correct and I can produce a short contract-friendly paragraph for v3.

- Snapshots/replicas: Our standard production backup cadence for dedicated/private customers is daily snapshots; replicas are geo-located to the same region (EU) unless customer enables cross-region DR. For the redline ask (30-day maximum for remnants) we need to confirm feasibility w/ infra — our usual SLA is "best-effort secure deletion of backup remnants within 30–45 days" because of immutable snapshot chaining and storage provider garbage collection windows.

- Hybrid/fallback: We can commit to EU-only fallback capacity for your account (contractual geofence) provided the project is configured with the EU-hosted fallback pool. Ephemeral KV caches are cleared on node termination and are not persisted to long-term storage; persistent caches (explicitly configured caching for embeddings/LLM KV) are considered persistent and included in the backup scope.

Action items: Markus — can you confirm whether we can tighten backup-remnant delete window to a guaranteed 30 days for Acme (account-level config + ops playbook)? Laura — can you draft the short clause that captures the geofence-only fallback and the definition of ephemeral vs persistent caches in contract language?

To Acme: we can set up a 30-min sync tomorrow to walk the specifics and show the erase-playbook.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-erase-playbook-2028.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: markus.klein@redwood.ai
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-21T13:45:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA: hybrid geofence + snapshot erasure safeguards — infra confirmation

Olga / Laura — quick tech note from infra:

- Backup architecture: Dedicated/private instances use region-scoped block snapshot chains. Snapshots are taken nightly (00:30 UTC) by default. Snapshot retention policy is configurable; the practical lower bound for complete garbage collection across our storage backend and provider-side retention hooks is 30 days, but edge cases (failed GC cycles, restored snapshots) can extend visibility of fragments up to 45 days.

- Account-level guarantees: For named enterprise accounts we can implement an account-specific retention policy and operational runbook that enforces a 30-day maximum for remnants in >99.9% of cases, with an explicit exception clause for lawful holds and for restoration rollback windows. We'll require an operational runbook (we can share) and a one-time migration script for existing snapshots if Acme wants immediate alignment.

- Ephemeral vs persistent caches: definition proposal — Ephemeral: KV caches resident only in RAM or local SSD and cleared on node termination; no replicated persistence. Persistent: caches explicitly configured with write-through to a durable store or replicated across nodes; these are included in backup scope. We'll produce a short definition paragraph for Laura to include.

I'll prepare the runbook excerpt and a short note that Laura can paste into the DPA, plus the migration checklist.

— Markus
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Svenja Müller <svenja.mueller@acme-payments.de>, olga.petrov@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-23T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA: hybrid geofence + snapshot erasure safeguards — redline Q&A

Hi Svenja — thanks for the patience. Summary and proposed contract language below (we kept it tight to avoid heavyweight addenda):

1) Backup & snapshot remnants
Proposed clause: "Redwood shall maintain backups and snapshots within the EU geofence for accounts designated with EU residency. Customer-initiated deletion requests will trigger Redwood's erase workflow. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to remove accessible backup remnants within 30 days of completion of the erase workflow; in no event shall this exceed 45 days except where: (i) a lawful hold applies, (ii) restoration or rollback of the customer environment is pending, or (iii) the customer has agreed in writing to an alternative retention schedule."

2) Hybrid fallback & geofence commitment
Proposed clause: "Where Customer configures Redwood for private deployment with EU geofence fallback, Redwood shall ensure that any fallback hosting or burst capacity used for the Customer's requests is provisioned exclusively in EU regions and will not replicate Customer data outside the EU geofence. This commitment applies for the duration of the contract term, unless prevented by force majeure or applicable law requiring cross-border transfer."

3) Ephemeral vs Persistent cache definition
Proposed clause: "For purposes of the DPA, 'Ephemeral Caches' are caches resident only in memory or on local node SSD that are cleared on node termination and are not written to durable replication storage. 'Persistent Caches' are caches configured to persist to durable storage or replicated across nodes and are treated as Customer data subject to backup and retention policies. Redwood shall document cache behavior in its operational playbook and make the playbook available to Customer under NDA for compliance review."

Next steps: 1) If this captures Acme's ask, Olga can push these three short paragraphs into the DPA v3 tracked-change file. 2) Markus will share the runbook excerpt and migration checklist (will attach). 3) We propose a 30-minute call Thursday 09:00 CEST to finalize.

Svenja — can you confirm acceptance of the language or flag any edits? If accepted, we'll update v3 and return a redline.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference
